what: Introduced the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act, which permanently bans large AI data centers and associated infrastructure on land owned or managed by the U.S., including military bases, and requires removal of existing qualifying data centers and site remediation.

name: Roger Marshall
what: At Semafor's World of Work event, said he does not want tax incentives for data centers or for them to 'drive up other people's electricity costs,' pointed to higher rates near Panasonic's Kansas plant as a warning, and said of Kansas counties' moratoriums: 'I certainly support their moratoriums,' adding those decisions belong at the local level.

name: Mike Lee
what: At the committee's FERC oversight hearing, Lee said he supported FERC's Large Load Order, called it 'not a one-size-fits-all solution,' and agreed that 'existing ratepayers should not subsidize the cost of data centers.'

name: James Talarico
what: Released a data-center plan at an Austin news conference: minimum federal requirements for grid, environment, jobs and transparency; repeal of the state data-center sales-tax exemption; large energy users pay their own infrastructure and grid interconnection costs; closed-loop water systems; local authority to approve and reject projects; release of facility-level tax-break records. He did not call for a moratorium. He said: 'Data centers are jacking up utility bills across the state of Texas.'

name: Shomari Figures
what: Cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (sponsor Rep. Ocasio-Cortez), added 07/22/2026.

name: Gabe Evans
what: Introduced H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, with Rep. Kathy Castor. It directs states and their PUCs to consider standards for connecting large-load customers so those customers, not families and small businesses, cover new generation, transmission and upgrade costs. Cleared House Energy and Commerce 52-0.

name: Kathy Castor
what: Sponsor, with Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO), of H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, which would require each state regulatory authority to consider a federal standard under which data centers and hyperscalers with demand of 100 megawatts pay the full cost of generation, transmission or distribution upgrades needed to serve them. Cleared the House Energy and Commerce Committee 52-0.

name: Lauren Underwood
what: Introduced H.R. 9825, the Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act of 2026. Its official title: to require data center operators to submit to States or the EPA Administrator and the Secretaries of Energy and Agriculture reports on data center energy and water use. Referred to House Energy and Commerce.

name: Mark R. Warner
what: Announced he is introducing the Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act: large AI data centers would publicly disclose energy and water consumption, emissions, backup generation and other operational impacts, and federal bonus depreciation would be conditioned on meeting efficiency and sustainability standards. The release says the bill is supported by the Chesapeake Bay Foundation, the Sierra Club and the Virginia League of Conservation Voters. No bill number is given on the page.

name: Mark R. Warner
what: Congress.gov lists Warner as sponsor of S.5054, the Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act of 2026, introduced 2026-07-21 and referred to the Senate Finance Committee (1 cosponsor). The same listing shows S.3682, the Power for the People Act of 2026, as sponsored by Sen. Van Hollen (introduced 2026-01-15), consistent with Warner being a cosponsor rather than the sponsor.
source_name: Congress.gov member page (filtered to 119th Congress, "data centers")

name: Terri Sewell
what: Announced cosponsorship of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, which would stop new construction and large expansions of AI data centers until a federal framework is established; said 'The bill simply says, let's put common sense guardrails in place before this expansion continues' and 'Responsible innovation and community protection are not competing goals—they are complementary ones.'

name: Mark DeSaulnier
what: Cosponsored H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

name: Lori Trahan
what: At the Energy and Commerce markup she supported passage of the Ratepayer Protection Act and the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (H.R. 6529). Said: 'If you build the data center, you pay for the data center.' Said both are 'good first steps' but 'don't fully address the water these facilities draw from our communities.'

name: Bob Latta
what: Statement on full Energy and Commerce Committee approval of H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act (July 21, 2026): said he spoke in support at the markup and that numerous states, including Ohio, already have large load tariffs in place for data centers.

name: Harriet Hageman
what: Cosponsored H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act (sponsor: Rep. Gabe Evans), joining on 2026-07-20; she is one of 42 cosponsors and not an original cosponsor.

name: Sanford Bishop
what: Said south Georgia communities need guardrails, transparency on water/power consumption, and community benefits before data centers move forward.

name: Austin Scott
what: Said computing 'is a big part of national security' and data centers should be in the U.S.; said 'We need to make sure that the companies who build the data centers are paying their own cost of energy' and that residents see no increased power costs. Said 'Closed-loop systems don't use nearly as much water as the old systems do. We need to make sure that we're talking about what kind of cooling systems they have.'

name: Alan Armstrong
what: Promoting his American Energy and Mineral Infrastructure Act, said "A manufacturer, a data center, an industrial facility will not commit billions of dollars to a region if it cannot obtain reliable energy at a competitive price."

name: Adam Hamilton
what: In KSHB's primary voter guide on data-center development, said the local community should decide whether a project goes ahead, that data centers should pay their own way, and that a data center's water use cannot come at the expense of drinking water or irrigation or raise a neighbor's bill.

name: Tommy Tuberville
what: Campaigning at an Alabama Sheriffs Association event, said opponents "are listening to all this nonsense they see on social media that's coming from China because China does not want us to grow," called environmental and noise objections "bull crap," and touted data center tax revenue for schools and law enforcement.

name: Charles E. Schumer
what: Told reporters that data centers should "pay their fair share and use more clean energy" and that Democrats would pursue data-center reform if they retake the Senate, adding "We know how important they are, and we've heard the message loud and clear."

name: Kirsten E. Gillibrand
what: Issued a statement supporting Gov. Hochul's executive order pausing hyperscale data-center construction for one year, saying New Yorkers need "ironclad guarantees that their energy bills won't spike, their water will be protected, and their air will remain clean."

name: Harriet Hageman
what: In a phone interview with Cowboy State Daily after her letter to Meta, said Meta called her office within 24 hours and that she joined a second call with Meta officials. She said she has encouraged Meta and other businesses coming to Wyoming to work with the communities where they intend to locate: talk with city leaders, hold public meetings and do public outreach. The paper reports she sees her approach on this less as a federal lawmaker and more as an advocate for Wyoming. (Evidence quote omits one short sentence, "Talk about what you intend to do.", to stay within 40 words.)

name: Emilia Sykes
what: Advanced the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 (H.R. 9497) in the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee; the release says the bill 'advances efforts to study the impact of data centers on regional water resources' but does not attribute that provision to her.

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Released a discussion draft of the Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act, which would require data centers to receive a federal certificate before permitting and construction affirming they will not harm the public interest and meet minimum energy, environmental and economic standards, and would fund grants to build community capacity.

name: Julia Letlow
what: Statement welcoming Meta's $50 billion expansion in Richland Parish, saying she was thrilled Meta was committing to cover the full cost and protect ratepayers.

name: Maxine Waters
what: Cosponsored H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

name: Jeff Van Drew
what: With Rep. Riley, introduced the FAIR Data Act, which prohibits utilities from passing grid upgrade costs for very large (75+ MW) data centers onto households and small businesses; said companies behind these projects should 'cover those added costs instead of passing them on to ratepayers'.

name: Josh Riley
what: Introduced the FAIR Data Act, bipartisan legislation to stop data-center projects from raising energy bills for Upstate New York families and small businesses by shielding ratepayers from the generation, transmission and distribution upgrades those projects require.

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Released 'The AI Accountability Agenda', which his office says includes new legislation requiring data centers to pay for necessary grid infrastructure and fund clean energy and storage to meet their capacity needs.

name: Sherrod Brown
what: Signal Cleveland reports that in a Spectrum News interview about two weeks before his first anti-data-center ad, Brown said the state should eliminate the data-center tax breaks, and that his campaign told Signal that Ohioans, not Husted, should decide whether data centers are built in their community. The story notes this put him at odds with building-trades unions that back the industry. (Gives the direct quote behind the 'has called to end the tax breaks' paraphrase already on file.)

name: Harriet Hageman
what: Sent a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg seeking answers about the discharge of the bacterium Cupriavidus gilardii into Cheyenne's municipal reuse water system from Meta's data center. Per her release, the Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities revoked the contractor's discharge privileges in March, residents were not told until the end of June, and local utility officials said drinking water was not threatened.

name: Harriet Hageman
what: Cowboy State Daily's report of her July 9 letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg quotes the letter itself (the earlier pass cited only her release): she wrote that many are rightfully concerned about high water consumption by data centers, that the contamination seemingly came from a closed-loop cooling system marketed as a solution to that, and asked among other things whether closed-loop cooling can scale down water consumption safely. SAME ACTION as the existing 2026-07-09 letter item - a second source with the letter's wording, not a second action.

name: Morgan McGarvey
what: Sent a letter to LG&E President John Crockett III opposing the hyperscale data center planned for Camp Ground Road and demanding existing ratepayers not bear the cost; release says the 400 MW facility is a 63% increase in demand.

name: Morgan McGarvey
what: LPM reported he told a forum he opposes hyperscale data center construction in Louisville and the state, and that residents should control what gets put into their community (headline: 'absolutely opposed'; his own quoted words: 'I am done with out-of-state corporations coming into our state, our home, our community, and using our resources').

name: Dina Titus
what: Letter to BLM (sent July 8) asking for 'robust public consultation and transparency' in permitting data centers on public land; said the BLM let a developer switch from a solar farm to a data center on federal land 'without any public review. This is unacceptable.'

name: John R. Curtis
what: Told Utah News Dispatch, citing distrust after the Stratos project's quick approval through the Military Installation Development Authority, that 'we do have some real uncertainty about these data centers. What's behind the meter? What's not?' and that 'something that I want to work on at the federal level is bringing some reliable, predictable measuring techniques' so the public has standard metrics; he said the industry had 'failed' at explaining why the facilities are needed.

name: Sherrod Brown
what: At a campaign stop in Ironton, asked about the federal plan for a 10-gigawatt data center near Piketon, said people locally were not told, that residents of Lawrence, Scioto and Pike counties should make the decision, and that people should not pay higher electric bills because of it.

name: Ron Wyden
what: Co-signed with Sen. Merkley a letter to Gov. Kotek's Oregon Data Center Advisory Committee raising energy demand, consumer electricity costs, water, noise, farmland rezoning, tribal consultation and transparency.

name: Jeff Merkley
what: With Sen. Wyden, wrote to Oregon's state data center advisory committee asking it to consider constituent concerns including rising energy demand, higher electricity costs for consumers, water quality and quantity, steam and noise from cooling, rezoning of productive agricultural land, tribal rights and consultation, and transparency.

name: Roger Marshall
what: Quoted in a KSHB voter guide ahead of the August 4, 2026 Kansas primary: 'Kansas isn't going to hand over our land, water, or power grid to Big Tech companies that turn a profit while local families foot the bill with taxpayer giveaways.'

name: Chuck Grassley
what: At a Q&A with Chesterman Company employees in Sioux City, asked about data centers, Grassley said 'These are state and local decisions to make,' and discussed their positives and negatives and possible legislation on their construction.

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Led, with Rep. Jennifer McClellan, a letter urging the EPA to withdraw a proposed rule that would let major polluting facilities, including data centers and fossil fuel plants, begin construction activities before securing Clean Air Act permits.

name: Brett Guthrie
what: Told WNKY: 'We can't have a moratorium that would cripple us. We also have to respect local communities and ensure these data centers pay their own way.' Said 'there's a good reason to be concerned' and developers should cover infrastructure costs.

name: Melat Kiros
what: Told Drop Site News she supports a moratorium on data center construction; said 'a federal data center moratorium is imperative and should be used as a negotiation tactic to implement significant regulation of AI.'

name: André Carson
what: In a release on the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (H.R. 9442, of which he is an original cosponsor) he said: 'Our bill would enact a pause until we can guarantee common sense protections.'

name: LaMonica McIver
what: Cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (sponsor Rep. Ocasio-Cortez), added 06/29/2026.

name: Kirsten E. Gillibrand
what: Asked about the proposed $19.5B STREAM data center at the STAMP site in Alabama, NY, said "People are worried about higher energy costs. They're worried about emissions. They're worried about polluting water," that communities should decide, and that developers should use closed-loop cooling and renewables rather than ratepayer-funded grid upgrades, while saying she lacked enough information to take a position on the project.

name: Shelley Moore Capito
what: E&E News reported that Capito said she is supportive of the concept of the Ratepayer Protection Act, and that while data centers are an 'important topic' with 'major pushback', the issue had not become part of the permitting negotiations she was leading. Reporter's paraphrase with two quoted phrases. (By November the permitting bill she co-authored did carry the Ratepayer Protection Act, per her own floor remarks already on file.)

name: Adelita Grijalva
what: Original cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

name: André Carson
what: Listed as a cosponsor of the House AI Data Center Moratorium Act in Ocasio-Cortez's release.

name: Jim McGovern
what: Listed among the cosponsors of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, which would institute an immediate federal moratorium on construction of new data centers and expansion of existing ones until Congress passes comprehensive AI legislation.

name: Frank Pallone
what: Called for a national AI data-center moratorium at an Energy Subcommittee markup — “in favor of a national AI data center moratorium until we can find a way to ensure they don't harm our nation's air, water, and power bills.”

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
what: Introduced the Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act, a temporary prohibition on construction of new data centers and expansion of existing ones until national safeguards (including that AI does not increase electricity and utility prices) are in place; requires reporting on water, energy, wastewater and wages.

name: Bob Latta
what: Statement after chairing the June 24, 2026 subcommittee markup: "We must ensure that American families are not left footing the bill for the significant grid upgrades and increased electricity demand driven by new AI infrastructure and other large load operations."

name: Troy Balderson
what: Co-introduced H.R. 9332, the Load Forecasting Enhancement Act, directing FERC to work with state PUCs on improving electric load forecasting as demand surges from AI and data centers. Passed Energy Subcommittee.

name: Martin Heinrich
what: In a Latitude Media interview reposted by his office, said data-center developers should follow SunZia's community-first approach, that "there's a healthy dose of arrogance in some of these" proposals, and that a developer should be able to tell a community "we're actually going to be able to lower your electricity bills."

name: Suhas Subramanyam
what: Introduced, with Reps. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) and Valerie Foushee (D-NC), the Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act, directing NIST in coordination with DOE to develop best practices and technical standards for measuring data center energy and water use, as a foundation for forecasting, planning and siting. "We need a simple way to track how much power and water these facilities use."

name: Cynthia M. Lummis
what: Introduced the POWER Up Act, which amends the Federal Power Act to clarify FERC jurisdiction over the interconnection of large-load facilities (projected peak demand of 100 MW or more) to interstate transmission, requires FERC to issue standardized interconnection procedures within 18 months, and explicitly preserves state and local jurisdiction over siting, permitting, construction, retail rates, local distribution and generation. Lummis: 'When a facility wants to draw as much power as a city, that is not an ordinary retail question. It is a grid question.'

name: Elizabeth Warren
what: Sent letters to KKR, BlackRock, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and Blackstone asking for details of their data center investments and how they ensure Americans are not left paying for them, with responses due June 27.

name: Marsha Blackburn
what: Posted a video questioning the location of DC Blox's proposed data center next to the Nashville Zoo and calling on the developer to 'revisit this placement,' while making clear she supports data centers more broadly.

name: John R. Curtis
what: Told Roll Call, on the Utah data-center uproar, 'I have almost no data on the water usage. I've heard it's closed-loop, but I don't know that,' called siting 'a local issue,' and said he was open to a congressional certification system for AI facilities similar to LEED building standards.

name: Abdul El-Sayed
what: Planet Detroit reported that in a May 28 primary debate he challenged a rival for supporting Michigan's data-center tax breaks, and that he told the outlet he would back legislation barring state and local tax breaks for data centers and ending nondisclosure agreements tied to them.

name: Brett Guthrie
what: Signed a letter with Reps. Joyce and Latta to the PCAST co-chairs and FBI Director Kash Patel expressing worries about 'foreign influence campaigns targeting artificial intelligence'; told the Daily News there is 'reasonable suspicion' that opposition is backed by China.

name: Tom Cotton
what: Wrote Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche asking DOJ to investigate foreign influence efforts, including by the Chinese Communist Party, targeting the buildout of U.S. AI infrastructure and public opinion on data centers. The same letter says Americans have valid concerns about energy costs and natural-resource strain from data centers and that 'common sense regulations and legislation' should protect communities.

name: Derek Schmidt
what: Per Ranson Financial's summary of a CJonline report: at a town hall gave three tips for communities: developers should not require tax abatements; data centers should source power from new or supplemental sources to avoid raising local utility costs; modern data centers can be designed as closed systems that do not consume large amounts of water.

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Reintroduced, with Rep. Don Beyer, the AI Environmental Impacts Act of 2026, which would require AI data centers to report environmental and energy-related impacts with fines for non-compliance, direct NIST to set measurement standards, and require an EPA lifecycle study.

name: Cory A. Booker
what: Cosponsored Sen. Markey's AI Environmental Impacts Act of 2026, which Markey's release says would require AI data centers to report on their environmental and energy-related impacts, with fines for those that fail to comply.

name: Bob Latta
what: Co-signed, with Chairmen Guthrie and Joyce, a letter to the PCAST co-chairs and FBI Director Kash Patel requesting information about evidence suggesting foreign influence campaigns are working to slow American AI progress and block data center infrastructure.

name: Troy Jackson
what: While running for governor, released an "Agency over AI" plan in Portland. Spectrum News reported the plan would require AI companies bringing data centers to Maine to build their own power sources and pay for grid upgrades, and that Jackson was among the candidates who said they would have signed the temporary statewide data-center ban Gov. Mills vetoed.

name: Mark R. Warner
what: Cosponsored the Power for the People Act with Sens. Van Hollen, Durbin, Blumenthal, Booker, Duckworth, Smith, Welch and Alsobrooks. Per his office the bill directs states to evaluate new rate classes for data centers, directs FERC to issue a rule on data centers paying for transmission upgrades, sets up an interconnection system rewarding data centers that bring their own new generation, use clean energy and pay prevailing wages, and funds better load forecasting.

name: Raul Ruiz
what: Letter to the Imperial County Board of Supervisors, read into the record by a district representative on June 2: "I unequivocally oppose data centers in Imperial Valley and urge local officials to prevent them from happening." Cited reduced life expectancy, air pollution, asthma, energy costs and water use. His office said he plans to send letters to EPA and DOE seeking federal oversight and environmental review of proposed projects in water-stressed environmental justice communities, including the Imperial and Coachella valleys.

name: Mike Lee
what: Told E&E News he had no immediate plans to take up data-center legislation: 'I don't currently have that identified as a priority,' while saying he was 'happy to look at' the Ratepayer Protection Act.

name: Chuck Fleischmann
what: As chair of the House Energy and Water Development Appropriations Subcommittee, said 'there will be no rate increases without going to the people' regarding TVA rate changes tied to data center demand.

name: Ben McAdams
what: UT-1 Democratic debate: all four candidates opposed the Stratos Project; said 'What we need are federal standards to make sure that when, as the economy is transformed, that the American people are the ones who benefit'. Opponents pointed to his financial stake in a data center project near Delta in Millard County; he said he was 'the only candidate who has worked to make a data center better by adding renewable energy' and described the stake as stock options and consulting pay from two years ago.

name: Gabe Vasquez
what: Told Source NM he encourages the county to approve the temporary moratorium it was considering on the proposed Socorro County data center, saying the proposal “should not be considered at this time.”

name: Harriet Hageman
what: In a Townhall.com interview (reposted on her House site), the columnist reports that, in the wake of backlash against data centers, Hageman said rising electricity demand can be addressed with abundant, reliable energy projects and done thoughtfully without ceding the AI race to China. That sentence is the columnist's paraphrase; Hageman's direct quotes are about reliable and affordable energy and do not use the words 'data center'.
source_name: Townhall (opinion column by Gabriella Hoffman), reposted on hageman.house.gov

name: Luke Bronin
what: The American Prospect wrote that, despite donations from billionaires with a stake in the data center build-out, Bronin “has called for regulation requiring data center developers to pay their fair share.” The article does not quote him or say where he said it.

name: Adam B. Schiff
what: Introduced the Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act: large-load facilities pay 100% of network upgrade costs, must demonstrate demand flexibility and provide their own power to interconnect, FERC to enable non-firm transmission service, and stronger interconnection screening against speculative projects. Schiff: "Hard-working Americans should not be left to foot the tab for rising energy costs. There needs to be guardrails that protect Americans' pocketbooks."

name: Katie Boyd Britt
what: Introduced the Advancing Water Reuse Act (S. 3585) with Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-NM): a tax credit for on-site water recycling at "manufacturing, food processing, and other industrial entities, including data center facilities"; Britt's statement cites water demand from "advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence, and other growth industries."
source_name: Sen. Luján press release (joint with Britt)

name: Ben Ray Luján
what: Introduced, with Sen. Katie Britt, the Advancing Water Reuse Act, a 30 percent investment tax credit for water reuse projects, covering onsite water recycling systems at manufacturing, food processing and other industrial entities, including data center facilities. The 2026 Congressional Record Index lists it as S. 4506, introduced by Luján.

name: Suhas Subramanyam
what: Introduced the Data Infrastructure Risk Reduction Act, directing DHS to produce a security strategy and recommendations for protecting communities around data centers, considering the security of transmission and water infrastructure.

name: Ruben Gallego
what: Told reporters in Phoenix data centers are a "necessary evil" for the AI race but "Your local resident should be held harmless. We shouldn't be paying more in electricity bills because data centers are here"; called for rolling back Arizona's 2013 data center tax exemption, said some data centers "end up paying, on average, less than some of the homeowners who are right next to them," and "I fear that we may not have enough water and we may not have enough power generation to be able to hold harmless everyone else."

name: Ben McAdams
what: Posted that 'Utah should welcome technology investment only when it aligns with our values: water stewardship, Great Salt Lake restoration, clean energy, transparency, public accountability, and real public benefit. This proposed data center project in Box Elder County does not meet that standard.'

name: Ron Wyden
what: Sent letters to the CEOs of Google, Apple, Meta and Amazon demanding answers on data-center water impacts in drought-prone Oregon (over 100 data centers), asking about closed-loop cooling, groundwater withdrawal, contaminant mitigation, public water tracking and community transparency, with a May 29 response deadline.

name: Chellie Pingree
what: Cosponsor of H.R. 8241, the Power for the People Act of 2026 (sponsor Rep. Tonko), added 04/30/2026.

name: Julie Fedorchak
what: At the Energy Subcommittee hearing 'AI and the Grid: Meeting Growing Power Demand While Protecting Ratepayers,' emphasized that those who drive the need for new energy infrastructure should pay for it (press release paraphrase), asked witnesses whether large loads such as data centers have shown willingness to pay for upgrades, and highlighted her FAIR Act and High-Capacity Grid Act.

name: Shelley Moore Capito
what: WCHS reported (paraphrase) that Capito said data-center companies must have early and strong community engagement and that transparency about the process and effects on residents could go a long way. In direct quotes she said proposed projects will build their own power behind the grid, so 'it won't impact it and it could actually maybe improve the situation because there will be excess power probably created,' and that the data center seeking to locate in Putnam County has guaranteed to replenish and clean the water it takes from the Ohio.

name: Steven Horsford
what: Release announced he would join OpenAI and Rep. Khanna at a College of Southern Nevada AI workforce-training event; says he helped secure almost $7 million for CSN's Westside Education and Training Center.

name: Nick Begich III
what: Op-ed: said Alaska's natural gas, renewables and stranded energy assets are an advantage for AI data centers; said the DATA Act protects ratepayers from subsidizing new loads; wrote 'We can hesitate, regulate too early and risk becoming an observer... or we can engage thoughtfully, strategically and on our own terms.'

name: André Carson
what: Original cosponsor (04/23/2026) of H.R. 8488, the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026, sponsored by Rep. McIver. Its text requires developers, 180 days before a definitive step, to disclose the site location and estimated resource needs and environmental impact to local elected officials and the public, and limits non-disclosure agreements.

name: LaMonica McIver
what: Introduced H.R. 8488, the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026 (04/23/2026). Its text requires developers, 180 days before a definitive step, to disclose the site location and estimated resource needs and environmental impact to local elected officials and the public, limits non-disclosure agreements, and requires a developer-funded independent environmental impact analysis.

name: Tim Kaine
what: Told E&E News he opposes a data-center moratorium: 'I think a moratorium would send the message to other nations, "Hey, the U.S. is giving up leadership in this space," and I don't want to send that message.'

name: Nick Begich III
what: Introduced the DATA Act of 2026 with Reps. Crenshaw and Owens; the release says it lets manufacturers and other energy-intensive industries run fully isolated off-grid power so 'innovation can scale without forcing households to subsidize massive new energy demands.'

name: Jon Ossoff
what: Wrote to FERC Chair Laura Swett announcing an investigation into AI data centers' potential impact on Georgians' power bills, asking for answers by June 1 to questions including whether FERC considers it credible and/or enforceable when technology companies say they will "pay their own way", what FERC is doing to improve load forecasting, how it will deal with load growth that exceeds predictions, and how it will take part in standardising interconnection for large loads like data centers.

name: Shelley Moore Capito
what: On her Thursday media call with West Virginia reporters (the call behind the WCHS item already on file, which is dated a week later), said community members should be heard early and that transparency is what communities need, while also saying there are 'wild accusations' about the downsides. MetroNews reports she said she does not believe data centers will create a lot of jobs but will create a lot of tax revenue.

name: Elizabeth Warren
what: With Sen. Hawley, wrote to the EIA administrator in March 2026 asking for a mandatory annual energy-use survey of data centers and other large loads; EIA then announced a mandatory data center survey to be completed by September 30, 2026. Warren: 'Americans deserve to know how much energy data centers are sucking up and what that's doing to their utility bills.'

name: Kweisi Mfume
what: Original cosponsor of H.R. 8241, the Power for the People Act of 2026, sponsored by Rep. Tonko; congress.gov gives its purpose as promoting data center load queues and data center-specific rate classes to mitigate the impact of data centers on other electricity consumers.

name: Paul Tonko
what: Sponsor of H.R. 8241, the Power for the People Act of 2026, introduced 04/09/2026. congress.gov gives its purpose as promoting data center load queues and data center-specific rate classes to mitigate the impact of data centers on other electricity consumers.

name: Roy Cooper
what: After a campaign speech in Fayetteville, told reporters data centers must pay their own way with no costs passed to consumers, and that local governments should have control and input over where they are sited.

name: Rick Scott
what: Introduced, with Sen. Roger Marshall, a concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge — under which tech companies commit to cover their own electricity and grid-infrastructure costs — is sound national policy. Scott: "Big Data centers are already putting a substantial financial burden on American families... Florida families shouldn't be supporting Big Tech companies' expansions with their electricity bills."

name: Roger Marshall
what: Introduced with Sen. Rick Scott a concurrent resolution supporting the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which tech companies commit to pay their own electricity and grid-infrastructure costs. Marshall: 'Kansans shouldn't have to pay higher utility bills so that big tech companies can power their data centers.'
source_name: Sen. Rick Scott press release (joint with Marshall)

name: Richard Blumenthal
what: As Ranking Member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, wrote public utility regulators in all 50 states requesting documents on non-disclosure agreements or other restrictions that keep data centers' energy use, water access, infrastructure strain and economic effects from public view: "American families deserve full transparency over Big Tech's expansion of data centers across the country and in their communities."

name: Mark Kelly
what: At the American AI Festival previewed unnamed legislation to "Bring developers and communities together at the beginning to work through the details—what a project means for energy, water, infrastructure, and jobs—and put real commitments on the table," with public input, enforceable agreements, local hiring and utility-rate protections.

name: Josh Hawley
what: With Sen. Warren, wrote EIA Administrator Tristan Abbey asking for a mandatory annual reporting requirement for data centers and other large loads covering hourly/annual/peak consumption, rates paid, upfront payments, demand response, and how transmission upgrade costs are allocated; response requested by April 9, 2026.

name: Martin Heinrich
what: At a Senate Energy and Natural Resources hearing on the power grid, said "new large loads, especially data centers, must bear the costs associated with them coming online" rather than shifting them to other ratepayers, and that 1% demand flexibility from large loads could unlock 126 GW of capacity.

name: Ruben Gallego
what: Co-leads (with Padilla, Hickenlooper, Cortez Masto, King) a draft Senate Energy Democrats transmission bill expanding FERC transmission authority; the senators' release does not mention data centers, though press coverage frames it as addressing AI data center demand.

name: Richard J. Durbin
what: Introduced the Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act (S. 4213), requiring data center operators to report energy and water consumption to their states, prospective facilities to report five-year estimates, and states to aggregate the data for EPA, DOE and USDA, with EPA fines for non-compliance. Durbin: 'If you've noticed a sharp increase in your utility bills lately, it may be from the growth of energy-hungry data centers.'

name: Mark R. Warner
what: At an Axios AI summit in Washington, said of a proposed data-center construction moratorium: 'That would be idiocy. A data center moratorium simply means China's gonna move quicker.'

name: Bernard Sanders
what: Announced the Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act of 2026 with Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez: a federal moratorium on new or expanded AI data centers until Congress enacts safeguards ensuring AI does not increase 'electricity or utility prices, harm communities or destroy the environment'; introduced as S.4214.

name: Greg Landsman
what: Introduced H.R. 8033, the No Harm Data Centers Act; official title: to ensure that American families are protected from the impacts of data centers on the electric grid. Referred to House Energy and Commerce.

name: Marsha Blackburn
what: Released a discussion draft of the TRUMP AMERICA AI Act that 'directs the U.S. Secretary of Energy to enter into agreements with owners and operators of data centers to protect consumers from rate increases and adverse impacts of data center development'; entities that decline become ineligible for federal incentives the Secretary identifies.

name: Mike Levin
what: With Rep. Sean Casten, led 120 House Democrats in introducing the Energy Bills Relief Act, which Levin said "ensures that data centers and large energy users pay their fair share instead of passing those costs onto families and small businesses."

name: Sean Casten
what: Co-led, with Rep. Mike Levin, the introduction by 120 House Democrats of the Energy Bills Relief Act; release lists 'Ensuring that facilities like data centers are paying for their own costs because it's not fair for their expenses to be pushed onto your household'. Casten's own quoted remarks do not mention data centers.

name: Bernie Moreno
what: Issued a release urging Carlyle Group to relinquish a $4.5M Ohio subsidy for Ark Data Centers' Akron/Independence expansion (10 jobs), sign the Ratepayer Protection Pledge and commit to more jobs, saying "When corporations like Carlyle demand massive amounts of electricity to fund their projects, it's everyday Ohioans who get stuck with the bill."

name: Chris Van Hollen
what: With Sens. Whitehouse and Heinrich, sent letters to Meta, OpenAI, xAI, Fermi America, American Intelligence & Power, Joule, Crusoe and Fundamental Data about twelve planned gas-powered data center projects, asking why they rely on gas, whether they will capture CO2, and their expected returns; responses due March 27.

name: Chris Van Hollen
what: At a Maryland delegation meeting on energy affordability: 'the surge of data center development across our region is only making things worse' and 'Consumers should not have to pay one dime in additional electricity costs to support data centers for the richest companies on the planet.'

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Wrote, with Sens. Blumenthal, Van Hollen and Booker, to the president of NARUC urging state utility commissions to protect residential and small-business ratepayers from data-center-driven rate hikes, including by rejecting rate filings that force ratepayers to subsidize data centers. The release contrasts this with the voluntary 'ratepayer protection pledge'.

name: Chris Van Hollen
what: Signed the Markey-led letter to the president of NARUC urging state utility commissions to reject rate filings that shift data center costs onto households and small businesses.

name: Cory A. Booker
what: Signed a letter with Sens. Markey, Blumenthal and Van Hollen to NARUC president Ann Rendahl urging state utility commissions to protect residential and small-business ratepayers from data-center-related rate hikes, including by rejecting rate filings that force ratepayers to subsidize data centers.

name: Adelita Grijalva
what: Cosponsored H.R. 7858, the Data Center Community Impact Act.

name: Rob Menendez
what: Listed as a cosponsor of the Data Center Community Impact Act, which would authorize a federal study of data centers' environmental, economic and public health impacts.

name: Summer Lee
what: Cosponsored H.R. 7858, the Data Center Community Impact Act.

name: Jon Husted
what: Attended a White House roundtable with President Trump, Energy Secretary Wright and tech executives at which Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft committed to the Ratepayer Protection Pledge to fund their own data-center power; Husted said "Requiring companies to fund their own power protects working people from higher bills."

name: Josh Hawley
what: Told Missourinet "I think we ought to say in the law that the data centers have to pay for their own electricity, the data centers have to pay for their own water supply," and that he does not want bills rising because "some corporation came in and sucked up all the power."

name: Ted Budd
what: At a Washington Post Live event said the U.S. needs to add about 85 gigawatts a year to keep pace with demand and "that goes back to permitting reform," that "power is good" and the country needs more energy, that data-center construction decisions should be made "at a local level," and was skeptical of Sen. Sanders' moratorium proposal while saying he would need to read the text.

name: Rich McCormick
what: Opening statement as chairman at the hearing 'Powering America's AI Future: Assessing Policy Options to Increase Data Center Infrastructure': called the Trump executive order prioritizing data center permitting 'a positive step', said several projects have faced substantial permitting hurdles, and asked whether a permitting framework 'largely designed in the 1970s' is suited to this infrastructure; also raised the question of whether residential ratepayers could end up subsidizing upgrades that primarily serve high-intensity users.

name: Emilia Sykes
what: At the House Science Committee hearing on data center infrastructure said: "We need to put strong guardrails in place so that data centers support our communities rather than the other way around. Ohioans should not pay higher electricity bills so billionaires in Silicon Valley can see higher profits." Noted Ohio has 217 data centers, the fifth most of any state.

name: Dan Sullivan
what: In his annual address to the Alaska Legislature, said he is pressing for "new federal data centers on Air Force bases in Alaska for AI computing," which he said would help the military, raise domestic demand for Alaska gas and lower the cost of building and financing the gas pipeline; noted the Air Force had issued a request for information on Alaska data centers the day before at his urging.
source_name: Sen. Sullivan press release (address to Legislature)

name: Josh Hawley
what: Introduced the Guaranteeing Rate Insulation from Data Centers (GRID) Act with Sen. Blumenthal, requiring data centers to obtain power from sources separate from the grid (10-year transition for existing facilities), giving consumers grid priority, and requiring public disclosure of electricity use; said "American families should not have to shoulder the burden of rising electricity costs produced by data centers."

name: Josh Hawley
what: Told St. Louis Public Radio, on introducing the GRID Act, that tech companies "can absolutely afford to pay for their own electricity, and they should," and that residents cannot know a project's effect on them "if they don't know exactly what the drawdown on power is going to be."

name: Emilia Sykes
what: Released the Affordability Agenda with the New Democrat Coalition; its energy section includes 'Reallocate electric grid costs to protect consumers from price hikes due to manufacturing and data center development.'

name: Steve Daines
what: Chairing a Senate Foreign Relations subcommittee hearing on European energy reform, said "whether it be for data centers, manufacturing, or defense production, reliable power is the backbone of our future prosperity."

name: John Boozman
what: At a Senate Environment and Public Works hearing on permitting reform, highlighted AI and cloud investments including the West Memphis data center and said "Arkansas was able to land these investments in part because of a reliable, affordable, and an all-the-above energy supply, including solar energy," backing permitting reform.

name: Sheldon Whitehouse
what: With Sen. Reed and four other New England senators, wrote ISO New England asking how it will shield residential ratepayers from data-center-driven price increases; said "As the ones who stand to benefit most, the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs."

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Joined Sen. Peter Welch and four other New England senators in a letter asking ISO New England how it will protect residential ratepayers from data-center-driven price increases. The letter, signed jointly, says the AI industry should be responsible for these costs.

name: Jack Reed
what: With Sens. Whitehouse, Welch, Shaheen, Blumenthal and Markey, wrote to ISO New England president and CEO Vamsi Chadalavada asking what strategies the grid operator will use to protect residential ratepayers from data-center-driven price increases. The letter says the senators believe tech companies, not American families, should be required to foot the bill for their load.

name: Peter Welch
what: Signed, with Sens. Markey, Shaheen, Blumenthal, Reed and Whitehouse, a letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada asking how the grid operator will protect residential ratepayers from data-center-driven price increases, stating 'the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs.'

name: James C. Justice
what: Press release applauding American Power and Intelligence Corporation's multi-billion-dollar data center and microgrid campus in Mason County, a project he first announced with Fidelis New Energy as governor in 2023: 'I truly could not be prouder to see the seeds of our work from years ago begin to bloom.'

name: Juliana Stratton
what: At the Sun-Times/WBEZ/University of Chicago Democratic primary debate, The Daily Line reported that the candidates agreed data centers are a good source of job creation, and that Stratton said more generation needs to be added to the grid to meet rising demand, pointing to the state law repealing Illinois's nuclear moratorium. Reporter's paraphrase.

name: Jeanne Shaheen
what: Signed, with Sens. Welch, Blumenthal, Reed, Markey, and Whitehouse, a letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada requesting the strategies ISO-NE plans to protect residential ratepayers from data-center-driven price increases, arguing that the AI industry, not families, should bear those costs.

name: Elizabeth Warren
what: Released the companies' responses: Google committed to pay for all electricity it uses and contribute to growth-related costs; Microsoft, CoreWeave and Equinix backed separate rate classes for data centers. Warren: 'These commitments do not explain how Big Tech companies – not American consumers – will bear the full cost of data centers.'

name: Ron Johnson
what: Told Wisconsin Watch that data centers' impact on the state's electrical grid is a 'very serious concern,' adding he is unsure local officials have 'really factored it in properly.'

name: Tammy Baldwin
what: Told Wisconsin Watch: 'The developers of these need to have commitments to the local community that they won't see, that they won't have to shoulder the costs of the energy use and water use by these data centers,' and said any data-center moratorium should first be considered by the state Legislature.

name: Raphael G. Warnock
what: Secured $50 million in the FY2026 government funding law to help communities address energy and water pressures from resource-intensive projects including data centers: "This bipartisan legislation will help give Georgians and Americans relief from the energy and water pressures of new resource-intensive projects."

name: Cory A. Booker
what: Cosponsored the Power for the People Act (Sen. Van Hollen's bill; the Congressional Record Index lists it as S. 3682 under Booker's cosponsored bills). His release says it directs states to evaluate new rate classes for data centers and directs FERC to issue a rule on data centers paying for transmission upgrades, with prevailing-wage and apprenticeship standards.

name: Cory A. Booker
what: Said in the same release that the costs of AI, especially higher electricity prices, must not be shifted onto working families in places like New Jersey, and that the bill ensures data centers pay the costs of their own development.

name: Tom Cotton
what: Told KATV that data centers drawing on existing grid generation would cause 'a price spike', and described the DATA Act as balancing affordable electricity for Arkansas families with encouraging data-center investment in the state.

name: Tina Smith
what: Named as an original cosponsor of Sen. Van Hollen's Power for the People Act, which directs states to evaluate data-center rate classes, instructs FERC to ensure data centers pay for local transmission upgrades, and creates an interconnection system pushing data centers to offset grid impact with new generation and storage under labor standards.

name: Mike Levin
what: Introduced, with Rep. Kathy Castor, the Stopping Hikes In Electricity from Large Load Demands (SHIELD) Act: a separate rate class for large load customers (facilities using more than 75MW) so households do not pay for their grid upgrades, plus priority interconnection for large loads powered by zero-emission electricity. "Families should not be forced to subsidize massive energy costs for billion-dollar companies."

name: Abdul El-Sayed
what: Campaign page "Terms of Engagement for Data Centers" lists eight conditions: no rate hikes, community transparency, energy reliability guarantees, a jobs guarantee with penalties, water protection through closed-loop cooling, binding community benefits agreements, no clean-energy loopholes, and enforceability through actionable penalties. The page does not mention a moratorium, tax breaks or federal legislation.

name: Abdul El-Sayed
what: Planet Detroit reported on the framework's release and that he told the outlet its priorities should be a guidepost for both local decisions and federal legislation, that federal legislation is needed because large tech companies target small townships, and that he is unlikely to get data-center legislation passed until President Trump leaves office.

name: Rob Menendez
what: Co-introduced the PRICE Act (require data centers to generate the electricity they consume; 75% renewable by 2035, 100% by 2040) and the Data Center Transparency Act (EPA quarterly and EIA semi-annual data collection) with Rep. Casar.

name: Greg Casar
what: Co-introduced the PRICE Act and Data Center Transparency Act with Rep. Menendez; quoted: 'Families should not pay more for utilities so that billionaires can get rich off AI data centers' and 'AI data centers should not be allowed to jack up your electric bill or poison your environment.'

name: Tom Cotton
what: Introduced the DATA Act of 2026 (introduced January 7; release dated January 8). Per his release it would exempt new, physically isolated off-grid electricity providers and certain consumer-regulated utilities from federal regulations, letting manufacturers, data centers and other energy-intensive industries build their own electricity systems, with eligibility limited to systems fully isolated from the bulk power grid.

name: Raphael G. Warnock
what: With Sen. Markey and five other senators, wrote FERC Chair Laura Swett urging the commission to prevent data center demand from producing unjust or unreasonable electricity cost increases for households, warning AI and crypto data centers could add over 10,000 MW of demand with costs passed to residential ratepayers.

name: Andy Barr
what: Senate campaign release on his coal plan says that as electricity demand from AI and data centers grows, reliable around-the-clock power is a national security issue, and lists among legislation he has 'led and supported' measures to speed permitting for power plants and transmission and to 'support AI data centers'. The release names no bill numbers.
source_name: Andy Barr for Senate press release

name: Michael F. Bennet
what: Campaign energy platform: "Massive energy users like data centers shouldn't drive up utility bills for Colorado families"; would "require new data centers to cover the cost of the energy they consume and to help finance the infrastructure they need," and require new projects to align with Colorado's clean energy, emissions, water conservation and workforce goals.

name: Catherine Cortez Masto
what: Submitted a $1,570,000 FY2027 community project request for the Desert Research Institute's Computing Infrastructure Evaluation Tool, "a cost-benefit framework to help Nevadans weigh trade-offs of rapid data center growth, considering water and energy resources, economic stability, and community well-being," plus $2,107,000 for a UNLV Energy Platform for Data Centers research project.
source_name: Sen. Cortez Masto FY2027 community project requests

name: Brian Schatz
what: In an interview on the Volts podcast, agreed ('100%') with the proposal that data centers needing grid capacity should fund distributed solar, storage and heat pumps on homes, and said it would be 'a rounding error' for highly profitable AI firms to also fund carbon dioxide removal.

name: Marsha Blackburn
what: Unveiled the TRUMP AMERICA AI Act national AI framework, which 'requires data center operators to be responsible for the full cost of all energy and water infrastructure needed for their operation, including construction, maintenance, and upgrades with no impact on ratepayers.'

name: Abdul El-Sayed
what: Told The Gander he would champion federal standards for data centers; the outlet reported he wants federal rules that ensure promised jobs materialise, require community benefits agreements, and make data centers pay for their own power without raising customers' rates. He also said data centers can bring good union jobs if done right.

name: Ruben Gallego
what: On the Volts podcast discussing his energy plan, said that if data centers strain the grid "the resident and the small business owner should not be having to pay the differential caused by these companies," that legislation should ensure "the individual consumer will be held harmless" while the large-load customer pays the difference, and that data centers should "bring your own energy" such as SMRs rather than restarting old coal or gas plants.

name: Richard Blumenthal
what: With Sens. Warren and Van Hollen, sent letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and three other companies probing whether "tech companies are passing on the costs of building and operating their data centers to ordinary Americans," including who bears grid-upgrade costs if the AI boom subsides.
source_name: Sen. Warren press office (in the news)

name: Elizabeth Warren
what: With Sens. Van Hollen and Blumenthal, sent letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix asking how they will keep data center grid costs off consumers' bills. Warren: 'Through these utility price increases, American families bankroll the electricity costs of trillion-dollar tech companies.'

name: Chris Van Hollen
what: With Sens. Warren and Blumenthal, sent letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix asking how they will prevent data center grid costs from being passed to consumers.

name: Rashida Tlaib
what: Statement after Southfield City Council approved a site plan for Metrobloks' proposed AI data center: cited residents' concerns about electricity costs rising 'by as much as 267%' and consuming 'millions of gallons of water per day', said she was inspired to see residents 'organizing together to push back', and said she would work with them to 'protect our communities'.

name: Maria Cantwell
what: Asked about environmental groups' call for a data-center moratorium, Cantwell said advocates 'should call for an above-all energy plan that allows for the construction of renewables to play into that demand for the future,' adding 'we're growing, so we need more energy sources.'

name: Greg Landsman
what: Introduced H.R. 6529, the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act, whose official title is to require FERC to hold a technical conference on protecting residential ratepayers from increased costs associated with large loads. Ordered to be reported by House Energy and Commerce on 07/21/2026.

name: Chellie Pingree
what: Spokesperson Gabrielle Maninno said Pingree believes Congress has a responsibility to assess the environmental and consumer impacts of data center and AI expansion and put 'strong, science-based protections in place'.

name: Ruben Gallego
what: Announcing his energy plan, said utilities are mostly regulated at the state and local level but the "federal government can invest in technology to divert energy from data centers during lulls in demand."

name: Derrick Van Orden
what: Told Wisconsin Watch: “The average Wisconsinite should not have to subsidize the power or water for a commercial entity” (said of manufacturers’ energy and water use, in a Foxconn story), and, of data centers, that they are “either going to help pay for those utility rates (that) are rising, or you’re going to self-power.”

name: Martin Heinrich
what: With Sen. Mike Lee, sent a bipartisan letter urging FERC to take up DOE's Section 403 proposal for a rulemaking on large-load interconnection; Heinrich called it "a step in the right direction" and said the rule should "ensure that households aren't left covering the increased demand from large new energy users."

name: Christopher A. Coons
what: Introduced the Liquid Cooling for AI Act with Sen. Dave McCormick: GAO to assess R&D needs for liquid cooling in data centers, DOE to evaluate the findings and report recommendations to Congress, and a liquid cooling advisory organization of industry experts. The release cites a Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report that data centers used 4.4% of U.S. electricity in 2023 and could reach 12.8% by 2028.

name: Adam B. Schiff
what: Co-signed letter with Sens. Markey, Van Hollen, Warren, Welch, Blumenthal and Warnock to FERC Chair Laura Swett urging the agency to ensure increased energy demand from data centers does not result in unjust or unreasonable rate hikes for American households.

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Wrote to FERC Chair Laura Swett, with six senators cosigning, urging FERC to ensure that energy demand from data centers does not result in unjust or unreasonable rate hikes for households.

name: Andy Barr
what: Introduced H.R. 5927, the Securing Reliable Power for Advanced Technologies Act (sponsor; 0 cosponsors listed; referred to House Financial Services). The bill would amend the Defense Production Act to let the President designate 'critical artificial intelligence infrastructure' projects as priority national defense projects with concurrent federal permitting on a consolidated schedule. Its definition covers AI data centers with at least 50 megawatts of connected load, dispatchable baseload generation of at least 100 megawatts that does not rely primarily on intermittent renewables and is committed to serve them, associated transmission, and fuel supply infrastructure including coal mines and gas facilities. The portion of the text read contains no ratepayer cost-allocation provision; the full text was not read to the end.

name: Cory A. Booker
what: Signed a letter led by Sen. Van Hollen and Rep. Beyer to PJM Board chair David Mills pressing PJM to put forward protections so customers do not bear the costs of rising data center energy demand; the letter says data center demand added over $16 billion in costs in the last two PJM capacity auctions.

name: Kevin Mullin
what: Led a group of 20 House members in a letter to FERC, Edison Electric Institute, and the Data Center Coalition expressing concern that data center energy costs are being passed onto consumers and requesting information on consumer protections.

name: Debbie Dingell
what: Named among the co-signers of the Mullin-led letters to FERC, the Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition raising concern that energy costs associated with data center development 'are increasingly being passed on to everyday Americans and small businesses' and requesting information.

name: Josh Hawley
what: After Missouri Senate President Pro Tem Cindy O'Laughlin called his data-center concerns misleading, said she "told me to stop asking questions about data centers and higher electricity rates. Not a chance."

name: Josh Hawley
what: Sent a letter to Ameren CEO Martin Lyons asking whether Ameren analyzed how discounted data-center contracts will affect residential prices and whether it prioritized household rate stability, saying Missourians "should not be forced to subsidize corporate projects while struggling to keep their lights on."

name: Michael F. Bennet
what: Co-signed (with Hickenlooper and four House members) a letter to Energy Secretary Wright on cancelled Colorado energy projects stating: "In an era where artificial intelligence and data centers are driving a rise in energy demand, we must meet these challenges by investing in responsible and affordable energy solutions, rather than destabilizing them."

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Wrote to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin opposing the decision to let major polluting facilities, including data centers and associated power generation, start pre-construction activities without required air quality permits.

name: Ted Cruz
what: Press release after touring Oracle and OpenAI's Stargate AI data center in Abilene: 'Texas is leading the way to make sure the United States beats China in the AI race. This is the beginning of a long-term effort to invest in American jobs, supply the additional power needed for AI, and deliver products and services that will benefit all Americans.'

name: Cynthia M. Lummis
what: Op-ed in Cowboy State Daily arguing Wyoming baseload energy should power U.S. AI data centers ('If we don't power America's AI with Wyoming energy, China will build their AI dominance on their coal instead'), citing 100 MW-plus AI training clusters; it does not address ratepayer or community impacts.

name: Troy Balderson
what: Led H.R. 1047, the GRID Power Act, directing FERC to let grid operators fast-track dispatchable power projects through interconnection queues. Cited data center growth in central Ohio. Passed the House.

name: Mark Kelly
what: Released the "AI for America" roadmap, noting data center power use could reach up to 12% of national electricity demand and proposing an AI Horizon Fund financed by AI companies; "As AI companies thrive, they must be good partners and invest in our workers, our economy, and our energy future."

name: Blake Moore
what: Introduced bipartisan 'Unleashing Low-Cost Rural AI Act' requiring DOE, Interior, and Agriculture to study how AI data center expansions impact rural America — energy supply, reliability, consumer costs, and infrastructure

name: Susie Lee
what: Toured Switch AI factory in Las Vegas with Democratic Leader Jeffries; said 'Switch is bringing the cutting edge of AI innovation right here to southern Nevada' and that the factories 'will help create good-paying jobs'.

name: Bill Hagerty
what: Quoted in Kairos Power's announcement of a deal under which its Hermes 2 plant in Oak Ridge supplies up to 50 MW to the TVA grid that powers Google data centers in Tennessee and Alabama; Hagerty said he was pleased to see the three join forces to deliver nuclear energy in Tennessee. His quote does not itself mention data centers.

name: John Barrasso
what: Senate floor speech praising the Trump AI Action Plan because 'it tears down barriers to building new data centers,' arguing that data centers need steady, reliable power and that more American energy means data centers grow in America rather than overseas.

name: Martin Heinrich
what: At a July 2025 ENR hearing on electricity demand growth, questioned Vantage Data Centers EVP Jeff Tench about how Interior Department reviews delaying wind and solar on federal land affect data-center business and grid reliability.

name: James E. Risch
what: At a Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee hearing, said he had doubted forecasts of AI-driven electricity demand but now expects the country to be 'inundated with demand for electricity', and pointed to nuclear generation as the answer. The release does not mention data centers by name.

name: Edward J. Markey
what: Hosted a virtual roundtable, 'The Data Center Next Door: Hidden Costs and Harms of Artificial Intelligence and Cryptomining', with Rep. Steve Cohen and community advocates, and released a storybook of residents' accounts of living near data center infrastructure.

name: Andy Kim
what: Introduced with Sen. Tim Sheehy the Advanced Reactor Modernization for Operational Resilience (ARMOR) Act of 2025, which authorizes up to 50-year military contracts for power from advanced nuclear reactors and, per the release, encourages "the co-location of AI infrastructure and data centers" at those installations.

name: Mike Lee
what: Chaired a Senate Energy and Natural Resources hearing on surging electricity demand, saying 'America's electricity demand is surging. We're entering a new era driven by data centers, AI computing, electric vehicles, and manufacturing returning home.'
source_name: Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee release

name: David McCormick
what: Hosted the Pennsylvania Energy and Innovation Summit with President Trump, where companies announced more than $90 billion in data-center, energy and workforce investments (CoreWeave $6B Lancaster, Blackstone $25B NE PA, ECP $5B York); the fact sheet mentions no ratepayer or community safeguards.

name: Rob Wittman
what: Supported the FY2026 NDAA committee text that “directs the Navy to use a promising partnership between Naval Weapons Station Yorktown and Dominion Energy as a pathfinder to determine how to leverage nuclear power to meet Navy and Marine Corps installation power demands, in addition to supporting the data center energy demands of accelerating technologies like artificial intelligence.”

name: Brian Schatz
what: Senate floor remarks: 'Energy demand is soaring for the first time in decades, largely not exclusively, but largely because of AI data centers,' arguing wind and solar are the fastest way to meet that demand; no position on who pays.

name: Bill Hagerty
what: In a Bitcoin Magazine interview, said Tennessee can become 'the energy hub of America' and that the state will see more mining operations, data centers and AI opportunities; the article paraphrases him as discussing building nuclear facilities to power mining and AI processing and citing xAI's Memphis operation.

name: James Talarico
what: Texas House Journal, third reading (final House passage) of SB 6: Talarico is listed as Absent on Record 3643, which passed the bill 103-25. No statement of vote from him on that record appears in the journal text read.

name: James Talarico
what: Texas House Journal, second reading of CSSB 6 ('relating to the planning for, interconnection and operation of, and costs related to providing service for certain electrical loads'): Talarico is listed among the Yeas on Record 3558, which passed the bill to third reading 117-24.

name: Cory A. Booker
what: With Sen. Andy Kim, led a letter from nine members of New Jersey's congressional delegation to PJM ahead of an anticipated 17% rate increase on June 1, 2025; the letter says the 2024 capacity auction results reflect growing grid demand from data centers and asks what PJM is doing to lower rates.

name: Andy Kim
what: Co-led, with Sen. Booker and seven NJ House members, a letter to PJM Interconnection ahead of a ~17% June 2025 rate increase; the letter attributes the 2024 capacity auction results to "the growing demand on the grid from data centers and advanced computer technology" and asks PJM what it is doing to lower rates, speed interconnection and prevent future price spikes.

name: Troy Balderson
what: At Energy and Commerce hearing, noted his district hosts Google, AWS, Meta, QTS, Vantage and others, with signed power agreements reaching 5,000 MW by 2030. Questioned Eric Schmidt about tech companies' role in bringing new generation capacity online.

name: Brett Guthrie
what: Washington Times op-ed (posted by E&C): argued for expanded energy production for AI data centers and permitting reform, warned about China; said 'common-sense, tailored protections may be necessary'.

name: Julie Fedorchak
what: Announced the next step of her AI and Energy Working Group, an RFI on AI energy demand with a topic titled 'Strategic Competition: Outpacing China.' Said: 'To be AI dominant, we must first be energy dominant.'

name: John Thune
what: Floor remarks 'Energy Security is National Security' warned that 'the boom in data center construction – in particular to power the rise of artificial intelligence – is placing, and will place, vast new demands upon the grid,' arguing for more conventional energy supply.
source_name: Senate Majority Leader Thune floor remarks

name: Mark Kelly
what: Co-signed a letter (with Sens. Van Hollen, Booker and Kaine) asking FERC to "host a technical conference" on ensuring sufficient new generation for data center demand while keeping rates affordable and respecting state energy policy.

name: Cory A. Booker
what: With Sens. Van Hollen, Kelly and Kaine, wrote to FERC asking the commission to hold a technical conference on ensuring the data center boom does not result in unjust and unreasonable electricity bills, service disruptions or increased fossil-plant pollution.

name: Sheldon Whitehouse
what: Led a letter with Sens. Schatz, Welch, Markey and Warren urging the Biden White House to reconsider a proposed executive order fast-tracking AI data-center construction, asking it to keep clean air and water standards and not prioritize tech companies' energy needs over households; said large companies "should not" be relieved of bringing new clean energy "while passing higher energy costs on to working families."

name: Shelley Moore Capito
what: On a call with statewide media, discussing an effort her office was involved in to bring a data center to Logan County, said 'We want them in West Virginia. They are massive investments, billions of dollars of investments,' and 'The appetite for power is going to be so huge. Everyone's going to win here.'

name: Lisa Murkowski
what: Introduced the Department of Energy AI Act with Sen. Joe Manchin; the bill directs DOE to "study the growth of computing data centers and the electrical power load." Her quoted remarks concern AI for science and permitting, not data centers.

name: Julia Letlow
what: Signed a nondisclosure agreement on June 29, 2024 with Laidley LLC, which Gulf States Newsroom describes as a shell company of Meta Platforms, covering Meta's plans for its Richland Parish data center, according to the document the newsroom obtained. The report says the NDA's definition of confidential information includes the existence of the agreement itself. Her spokesperson said NDAs are common in economic development discussions and that this one was limited to protecting preliminary business information. (The same story reports her later Meta and Nvidia stock trades and late disclosures; her spokesperson said she did not direct the trades and was unaware of them.)
source_name: Gulf States Newsroom via Louisiana Illuminator

name: Roger F. Wicker
what: Statement on the groundbreaking of Amazon Web Services' $10 billion, two-campus hyperscale data-center project in Madison County, calling it "a historic investment in our state" and pledging to keep Mississippi attractive to business.

name: John Hoeven
what: Letter read at Applied Digital's Ellendale data-center energizing ceremony saying "technology is serving as the third wave of our state's economic growth following expansion in agriculture and energy" and that the facility provides infrastructure and computing capacity across industries.

name: Kevin Cramer
what: Letter read by his constituent-services representative at Applied Digital's Ellendale data-center energizing ceremony, saying that with North Dakota's "wide open spaces, abundant energy and ideal climate, there is a bright future for additional development within our state."

name: Steve Daines
what: Announced at his Montana 'On the Rise' Economic Summit a Bitzero investment to build a 50 MW data center powered by Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes hydropower, saying it would "support good-paying jobs in Montana" and keep the state "at the forefront of the energy and technology sector."

name: Pete Ricketts
what: As governor, signed LB 1150, which lets certain "tier two" data centers apply for sales and use tax exemptions on some equipment purchases and rentals. Source is a tax-industry summary that names him as the signing governor, not the Legislature's own bill page.

name: Mike Crapo
what: Statement in the Idaho Commerce announcement of Meta's $800 million Kuna data center: 'This is a promising step for job growth and opportunities in the community,' noting the center is expected to be supported by renewable energy.
source_name: Idaho Department of Commerce press release

name: James E. Risch
what: Statement in the Idaho Commerce announcement of Meta's Kuna data center welcoming it as a source of jobs.
source_name: Idaho Department of Commerce press release

name: Susan M. Collins
what: Joined Sen. King at the Millinocket celebration welcoming Nautilus Data Technologies' water-cooled, hydro-powered data center to the former Great Northern Paper mill site, calling it "one of the greenest facilities in the world."

name: Angus S. King, Jr.
what: Joined Sen. Collins at the Millinocket celebration welcoming Nautilus Data Technologies' water-cooled, 100% hydro-powered data center to the former Great Northern Paper mill site, saying "sustainable projects like this are the blueprint for Maine's future" and "create good jobs that strengthen our communities."

name: Pete Ricketts
what: As governor, spoke at the groundbreaking of Google's $600 million data center in Papillion, saying he hoped it would rival Google's data centers in Iowa and crediting the state's workforce.

name: John Hoeven
what: Spoke at the groundbreaking of Midco's $12 million Tier III data center in Fargo, calling fast, secure data services vital across energy, health care, and other sectors and the facility important infrastructure for attracting national companies.

name: Pete Ricketts
what: As governor, announced that Facebook had selected Papillion for a data center and tied it to his administration's priority of growing the state's tech industry. The release does not mention tax incentives or legislation.

name: Tammy Duckworth
what: Cosponsored the Power for the People Act, making data-center operators pay the grid costs they create.
source_name: Sen. Welch joins bill so Americans aren't footing big data-center costs (2026)
